Convert data for unmarked::occuFP()

Source: R/fp_to_unmarked.R
fp_to_unmarked.Rd

Turns an fp_data object into the unmarkedFrameOccuFP that unmarked::occuFP() fits by maximum likelihood, the frequentist counterpart of fp_occu() (see vignette("unmarked")). With occasion = "occasion" it is the reverse of fp_data_wide().

Usage

fp_to_unmarked(data, obs_covs = NULL, occasion = NULL)

Arguments

data

An fp_data object, for instance built with fp_aggregate() and fp_data() from fp_read_sheepdog().

obs_covs

Optional names of numeric columns of data$auto to pass as observation covariates.

occasion

Optional name of a column of data$auto (and of data$verified, if it has one) that numbers the occasions. Each occasion then goes to the column of its rank among all the values, so that occasions missing at a site leave NA in their place. Without it, a site's occasions are placed in the order of their rows.

Value

An unmarkedFrameOccuFP object.

Details

The detection matrix has one row per site, in the order of data$sites, and the verified occasions first: type = c(n_verified, n_automated, 0), where n_verified and n_automated are the numbers of verified and automated occasion columns (see occasion); sites with fewer occasions get NA.

The observation covariate METH is "verified" on the verified columns and "auto" on the automated ones (the reference level), because occuFP() describes true detection by both methods with one formula: use detformula = ~ METH for a separate detection probability of the verified method, as fp_occu() has. The covariates in obs_covs exist for the automated occasions only; they are 0 on the verified columns, because occuFP() drops every observation whose covariate is missing. Centre them, so that 0 is a typical value, and read a covariate in detformula as acting on the automated method.

Recorders are not passed on (occuFP() has no random effects), and data of the observation-confirmation design (confirmed in fp_data()) are not supported.

Experimental

This function is experimental (new in 2.0.0, part of the integration with 'sheepdog'): its arguments and results may change in a minor version. See crywolf-api.

See also

fp_data_wide(), vignette("unmarked")

Examples

sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 200, nocc = 10, seed = 1)
umf <- fp_to_unmarked(sim$data, occasion = "occasion")
unmarked::occuFP(detformula = ~ METH, FPformula = ~ 1, stateformula = ~ x,
                 data = umf)
#> 
#> Call:
#> unmarked::occuFP(detformula = ~METH, FPformula = ~1, stateformula = ~x, 
#>     data = umf)
#> 
#> Occupancy (logit-scale):
#>             Estimate    SE      z  P(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)    0.061 0.151  0.404 0.686182
#> x             -0.516 0.156 -3.303 0.000956
#> 
#> Detection (logit-scale):
#>              Estimate     SE     z  P(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)     0.381 0.0681 5.589 2.28e-08
#> METHverified    0.222 0.2499 0.888 3.75e-01
#> 
#> false positive (logit-scale):
#>  Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
#>     -2.84 0.161 -17.7 6.34e-70
#> 
#> AIC: 2165.575 
#> Number of sites: 200
#>
